**Finding: Compliant** (rule T4C — Termination for convenience)

**Where it lives:** Despite the outline showing no term/termination heading, the operative provisions are embedded at the tail of the § 12 block — Section 13 (Term, p0078) and Section 14 (Termination, p0079). The planner's "likely absent" hint was incorrect; sec-2 only cross-references ("The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12") and sec-5 contains no early-termination fee.

**Why it clears the preferred position:**
- **Customer exit:** Section 14 lets Client terminate at will on written notice, with services and charges running only to the last day of the month following the notice month — effectively 30–60 days, inside the preferred 30-day band.
- **No penalty:** No early-termination fee anywhere. Fees are invoiced monthly in arrears (§ 5(a), paid within 15 days of receipt), so there is no prepaid-fee exposure and the missing pro-rata refund mechanic is immaterial — noted in the rationale, not redlined.
- **Vendor has no mid-term convenience right:** Section 13's early triggers are Client breach/default (for cause). The only other exit is a *mutual* 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year term.

**Two minor sub-elements noted, deliberately not flagged:**
1. No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — neutralised by arrears billing.
2. Vendor's non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the fallback's 90. This is an end-of-term non-renewal (which the fallback permits), the term is 12 months rather than multi-year, and critically the right is symmetric — we hold the identical 30-day right. Redlining it would cut down our own flexibility, so it is not worth the leverage.

Consistent with the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party, no redline was proposed and none was validated.
